Three things are outside the scope. The computation of a proven acceptable range itself, which is how the other parameters are held or varied while one parameter is scanned, is not reviewed here. The experiments themselves are not reviewed either. Finally, the study deviations recorded in the step reports keep the disposition those reports give them.

The re-analysis in §6 uses the same designed experiments and the same results as Version 1.0, with two additions. The first is the fragment results by nrCE-SDS of the designed experiments. They were measured before Version 1.0 was approved (§4.7), `{python} ce_where_txt`, but Version 1.0 did not report them. The second is `{python} n_sdm_sup` further set-point runs of the Protein A scale-down model (study `{python} sdm2_id`), made from `{python} sdm2_start` to `{python} sdm2_end`, during the investigation.

The Protein A plan, PCP-005, had planned `{python} n_sdm_planned` set-point runs for the qualification of that model (study `{python} sdm1_id`). The further runs were made during the re-analysis, to narrow the confidence interval of the offset of the model for pool host cell protein. Of the Protein A pool attributes, host cell protein comes nearest its criterion of `{python} big(pa_hcp_v2)` ng/mg. On the model that PCR-005 Version 2.0 uses, its upper 95 % prediction limit over the NOR as characterized is `{python} f"{pa_hcp_use:.0f}"` % of the criterion, and it rises with `{python} pa_hcp_drivers`. That model is fitted on the log scale, so the offset is a difference of mean logarithms. It is stated as a ratio, the geometric mean of the scale-down runs divided by that of the manufacturing-scale batches. On the planned runs alone, the ratio is `{python} pa_r_plan`, with a `{python} OFF_CI` % confidence interval of `{python} pa_r_plan_lo` to `{python} pa_r_plan_hi`. On all runs it is `{python} pa_r_all`, with an interval of `{python} pa_r_all_lo` to `{python} pa_r_all_hi`. The plan did not foresee the further runs, so the Protein A report PCR-005 Version 2.0 records them as `{python} pd_id`, a discrepancy from the plan. They are not a deviation, because no approved procedure or GMP requirement was departed from.

A scale-down model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of that interval (§6.1). Over the NOR as characterized, the model is not qualified for pool host cell protein, on the planned runs alone or on all runs. With the ratio at the low end of its interval, which raises the prediction at manufacturing scale, the upper prediction limit over that NOR is `{python} big(pa_upl_char_lo)` ng/mg on all runs, above the criterion. The Protein A report PCR-005 Version 2.0 therefore `{python} pa_nor_txt`. Over the narrowed NOR, that limit is `{python} big(pa_upl_force_lo)` ng/mg on all runs, and the model is qualified. On the planned runs alone it is `{python} big(pa_upl_force_lo_plan)` ng/mg, and the model would not be qualified. The further runs therefore made the qualification possible. The decision to make them was taken after the result on the planned runs was known. The qualification therefore rests on runs added after a result was seen, and this is a limitation of it. The qualification rule and the criterion were not changed, and only the number of runs grew. For `{python} lpa_oname` the model is qualified on either set of runs.

# Background

## The master plan

PCMP-001 Version 1.0, the master plan, required that each step be judged against a criterion that applies to it. It did not say how that criterion was to be obtained. Its §7 left the threshold to the step plans.

> Where a threshold depends on the step, on the attribute or on the precision of the method, the criterion is defined in the plan of that step and the reason is given there.

The same section stated that the criterion for a response is the in-process limit of the step where one has been established, and the drug-substance criterion where none has. It gave neither a rule nor a value for an in-process limit.

## The Protein A analysis

The need for step criteria became apparent during the analysis of the Protein A study. The capture pool carries host cell protein at a level far above the drug-substance criterion of `{python} big(ds_hcp)` ng/mg. Protein A capture removes most of the host cell protein of the harvest, and part of the remainder is carried into the eluate bound to the antibody. That level is acceptable in an intermediate, because cation exchange and anion exchange remove most of it afterwards. Judged against the drug-substance criterion, no part of the Protein A characterization range would have been acceptable. PCMR-001 Version 1.0 put the argument in one sentence.

> The drug substance limit is the wrong yardstick for an intermediate, and the campaign uses a criterion for each step that applies to that step.

## The Version 1.0 criteria

Version 1.0 set `{python} n_r1` step criteria at `{python} n_r1_steps` steps, by four rules. @tbl-criteria-change gives each criterion with its rule code, beside the Version 2.0 criterion that replaced it. The Version 2.0 columns are discussed in §6.

1. For an impurity that downstream steps clear, the drug-substance criterion was carried back through the clearance the downstream steps delivered at their set-points in this campaign. The result was divided by a safety factor (R1, `{python} n_margin` criteria).
2. For an attribute that no downstream step changes, the criterion was an alert limit at the capability mean plus `{python} f"{sigma:g}"` SD (R2, `{python} n_capbased` criteria, all at the bioreactor).
3. For viral clearance at low-pH viral inactivation and anion exchange, the criterion was the cumulative requirement less the nominal clearance of the other credited steps (R3, `{python} n_viral_req` criteria).
4. For viral clearance at virus filtration, the criterion was the nominal clearance claimed for the step less `{python} f"{v_allow:g}"` log10 for assay variability (R4, `{python} n_viral_claim` criteria).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.criteria_change().show()
```

The back-calculation through nominal downstream clearance, the viral criteria less the other steps' nominal clearance and the virus filtration criterion less the assay allowance all rest on the nominal results of this campaign. The alert limits rest on its capability data. Every Version 1.0 criterion was therefore set after the data were seen, from this campaign's nominal performance or capability, and where a safety factor was used its size was chosen step by step.

# Investigation

## Approach

The sequence in which the criteria were set was reconstructed from the analysis records, from the study chronology and from the authors of the Version 1.0 reports. Each criterion in @tbl-criteria-change was recomputed from its stated rule and compared with the value printed in the documents. The capability assessment was repeated against the drug-substance criteria as the register prints them. The execution windows of the studies were compared with the calibration records of the equipment they used. The record of the fragment method was reviewed against the decision `{python} AMD["id"]` to measure fragments by nrCE-SDS and against the comparability study S-CEX-FRC. Every recomputed criterion agreed with the printed value.

## F1. Criteria defined after the data were seen

The step criteria were defined after the data were seen and outside the approved protocols.

Each step plan was approved before its studies began, as @tbl-plan-dates in §4.6 shows. The Protein A plan PCP-005, for example, was approved on `{python} pa_appr`, and its first study started on `{python} pa_first`. None of the step criteria was in a plan as approved. The criteria were introduced later, while the Protein A data were being analysed, when it became clear that the capture pool could not be judged against the drug-substance criterion (§3.2). They were then written into the text of every step plan when the Version 1.0 package was compiled. The approved plans were not revised to carry them. The Version 1.0 plans therefore read as if the criteria had been approved before execution.

The master plan PCMP-001, approved on `{python} pcmp_appr`, did not prevent this. As §3.1 shows, it required a step criterion without fixing one. The record therefore holds no protocol, approved before execution, that contains a step criterion. A criterion added to a protocol after its data are known does not meet the purpose of a protocol [@fda2011].

## F2. Safety factors chosen so that each step passed at its set-point

For an impurity that downstream steps clear, Version 1.0 carried each drug-substance criterion back through the nominal downstream clearance of this campaign and then divided it by a safety factor (R1 in @tbl-criteria-change). The factors ranged from `{python} f1(m_lo)` to `{python} f1(m_hi)`, and no document records why they differ.

@tbl-margins sets each factor against the value that the response surface model of the step predicts at its set-point. The last column gives the largest factor at which that set-point value would still have met the criterion. Every step meets its Version 1.0 criterion at its own set-point. Had the largest factor used, `{python} f1(m_hi)`, been applied to every step, the set-point value would have failed its criterion for `{python} n_fail_uniform` of the attributes in @tbl-margins. The analysis records show that a factor was reduced where the limit would otherwise have fallen below the value the step produces at its set-point.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(margin_show,
        caption="Safety factors of the Version 1.0 step criteria against the value each step produces at its set-point.",
        label="tbl-margins", merge=["Step"], header=margin_header, notes=margin_notes,
        align=["P{2.4cm}", "P{3.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"]).show()
```

The highest pool level in @tbl-margins assumes that every downstream step clears as much as it does at its set-point. A downstream step that runs elsewhere in its NOR may clear less, and the downstream steps can then bring a lower pool level within the drug-substance criterion. Version 1.0 divided each criterion by a safety factor to cover this. The factor was chosen. It was not calculated from how much less the downstream steps clear within their NORs.

The Version 1.0 viral clearance criteria for low-pH viral inactivation and anion exchange rest on nominal clearance in the same way. Each was the cumulative requirement less the clearance of the other two steps in the viral clearance summary of Version 1.0. That summary gives a single value for each step and virus, at the set-points. For XMuLV it gives `{python} vcs_xm_txt`. For MVM it gives `{python} vcs_mvm_txt`. The Version 1.0 XMuLV criterion for low-pH viral inactivation, for example, was `{python} vcs_example`. The Version 1.0 virus filtration criteria were the virus filtration values of the same summary less `{python} f"{v_allow:g}"` log10. None of these summary values is a mean of the response surface models in @tbl-viral.

## F3. Capability limits judged against the data they came from

For the glycans and acidic variants, Version 1.0 set `{python} n_capbased` bioreactor criteria at the mean plus `{python} f"{sigma:g}"` SD of the commercial-scale capability simulation (R2 in @tbl-criteria-change). @tbl-cap-limits recomputes each one. The recomputed value and the printed criterion agree to the second decimal place.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cap_show,
        caption="Version 1.0 bioreactor criteria recomputed from the capability data. Mean and SD are those of the simulated drug substance at commercial scale.",
        label="tbl-cap-limits",
        header={"Capability mean": "Capability\nmean", "Capability SD": "Capability\nSD",
                f"Mean + {sigma:g} SD": f"Mean +\n{sigma:g} SD",
                "Version 1.0 upper criterion": "Version 1.0\nupper criterion",
                "Drug-substance criterion": "Drug-substance\ncriterion"},
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"]).show()
```

The capability simulation draws every parameter inside its NOR. The proven acceptable range analysis then asked whether the upper 95 % prediction limit stayed within the alert limit while the other parameters varied inside the same NOR. For a normal distribution, about `{python} f2(exceed_pct)` % of the batches lie above a one-sided limit at the mean plus `{python} f"{sigma:g}"` SD, whatever the process. A limit of this kind is an alert limit for trending. It is not an acceptance criterion, because it carries no information about what the product needs.

An alert limit of this kind can be reached inside the NOR by a batch that is well within the drug-substance criterion. The bioreactor report PCR-003 Version 1.0 reported such a case, a corner of the NOR at which predicted afucosylation exceeded its alert limit while meeting the drug-substance criterion by a wide margin. For the same reason, several proven acceptable ranges at the bioreactor stopped short of the NOR because they reached an alert limit, not the drug-substance criterion (§6.3).

## F4. Acidic variants assessed against one end of a two-sided range

The register gives acidic variants a two-sided criterion of `{python} f"{ds_acid_lo:g}"` % to `{python} f"{ds_acid_hi:g}"` %, and the Version 1.0 capability table printed that range. The capability index beside it was computed against the upper end alone and printed as `{python} f1(acid_cpu)`. The simulated drug substance has a mean of `{python} f1(acid_mean)` % and an SD of `{python} f2(acid_sd)` %. Computed against both ends, the index is `{python} f2(acid_cpk)`, because the mean lies `{python} f1(acid_z_lo)` SD above the lower limit and `{python} f1(acid_z_hi)` SD below the upper limit. The same one-sided treatment was used in the proven acceptable range analysis. @tbl-criteria-change records the Version 1.0 alert limit for acidic variants as an upper limit only, and PCR-003 Version 1.0 judged its acidic variant ranges against that upper limit alone.

Two statements in PCMR-001 Version 1.0 rested on the one-sided capability index. It reported the lowest capability index of the drug substance as `{python} f2(v1_min_cpk)`, for `{python} v1_min_name`. A capability index for a validated clearance claim, computed per batch, has no clear meaning, and it is quoted here only as PCMR-001 printed it. PCMR-001 also reported that no simulated batch fell outside an acceptance criterion. Against both ends of the acidic variant range, the simulation puts `{python} noos_phrase` outside it.

## F5. Approval and execution dates missing from the records

The Version 1.0 records misstated when the plans were approved and did not state when the studies ran. Every Version 1.0 title block carried the date `{python} REV1_DATE`. That was the approval date of the reports and the date on which the package was compiled. For the plans, it replaced the date of approval. @tbl-plan-dates sets the approval date of each plan against the start of its first study. Every plan was approved before its first study began. Read from the title blocks, every plan appeared to have been approved after its studies had started.

Their equipment tables recorded each instrumented system as in calibration at execution and gave the next calibration due date. `{python} due_phrase` A reader of the record could not confirm calibration at the time of use, and the tables appeared to cite expired calibrations.

The execution windows were recovered from the study records. @tbl-calibration gives them for the `{python} n_cw_studies` studies that ran on the `{python} n_cw_eq` instrumented systems. Every one of these studies closed before the calibration of its system fell due. The smallest margin is at study `{python} cw_near_study` at the `{python} cw_near_step` step, on the `{python} cw_near_desc` `{python} cw_near_eq`. It closed on `{python} cw_near_end`, `{python} cw_near_days` days before the calibration due on `{python} cw_near_due`.

## F6. Fragments by SEC in the Protein A and low-pH viral inactivation pools

In the comparability study S-CEX-FRC at cation exchange, executed from `{python} frc_start` to `{python} frc_end`, fragments were measured by SEC and by nrCE-SDS on the same samples. @tbl-sec-cesds gives every replicate.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.method_comparability().show()
```

On average, SEC read fragments higher than nrCE-SDS by `{python} f2(d_up_lo)` to `{python} f2(d_up_hi)` percentage points in the Protein A pool, the VI pool and the CEX load. From the CEX pool onward, the mean difference between the two methods was no more than `{python} f2(d_dn_abs)` percentage points. The difference follows the host cell protein content of the sample. Part of the host cell protein elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC, where it is counted with the clipped antibody species. The excess can therefore be no larger than the host cell protein in the sample. Cation exchange removes most of the host cell protein, and from its pool onward the excess is close to zero. In the Protein A pool, SEC reported a mean of `{python} f2(sec_pa)` % fragments, where nrCE-SDS reported `{python} f2(ce_pa)` %. The excess there is about `{python} f"{d_pa_share:.0f}"` % of the fragment level that nrCE-SDS measures, and about `{python} f"{sec_share_crit:.0f}"` % of the Protein A fragment criterion of `{python} f2(pa_frag_crit)` % (@tbl-iac). SEC fragment results from the Protein A pool and the low-pH viral inactivation pool are therefore biased high by an amount that would use a large part of a fragment criterion.

The decision `{python} AMD["id"]` to measure fragments by nrCE-SDS was taken on `{python} AMD["date"]` on these data. From that date, fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS in every study, at every step, so that one method spans the train. The CEX response surface study, which ran from `{python} cexr_start` to `{python} cexr_end` and so spanned the decision, measured fragments by both methods in parallel. The retained response surface samples of Protein A and viral inactivation were retested by nrCE-SDS from `{python} ret_start` to `{python} ret_end`. The screening samples had not been retained. Their SEC results are kept and marked as not used. The re-executed anion exchange design (DEV-008-01) started on `{python} aexr_start`, after the decision, and measured fragments by nrCE-SDS. Its invalidated first execution had used SEC. Fragments were not in the scope of the bioreactor design. @tbl-methods-by-study shows which method ran in which study.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study().show()
```

The decision `{python} AMD["id"]` and the nrCE-SDS retests predate Version 1.0. However, the Version 1.0 documents did not report fragments, their register carried no fragment attribute, and none of them cited `{python} AMD["id"]`. No procedure required that a method decision taken during a campaign be assessed against the approved plans and, where it changed them, be put into effect by a plan amendment. The decision to measure fragments by nrCE-SDS therefore never reached the documents.

# Root cause

The root cause is that PCMP-001 Version 1.0, the master plan, required a criterion for each step but gave no rule for deriving one (finding F1). When the Protein A analysis showed that an intermediate cannot be judged against a drug-substance criterion, the criteria were derived during the analysis, by the people analysing the data, with the results in view. Every rule they chose drew on the nominal results or the capability data of the studies being judged (§3.3).

Four causes contributed.

1. SOP-1002 did not require that the acceptance criteria and their basis be approved in the protocol before execution. Criteria set after execution could therefore be added to the plan text when the package was compiled, without a revision of the approved plan (finding F1, criteria defined after the data were seen).
2. Neither the plans nor the master plan defined how much less a downstream step may clear within its NOR, which is what a step criterion has to allow for. A chosen safety factor was used instead, and its size was set step by step (finding F2). Capability data were used where no downstream step changes the attribute (finding F3).
3. No second review checked whether a capability calculation used a one-sided or a two-sided criterion as the register gives it (finding F4, acidic variants). No second review checked the dates in the title blocks and study records against the approval and equipment records (finding F5).
4. No procedure required that a method decision be assessed against the approved plans and put into effect by plan amendment (finding F6, fragments by SEC).

# Impact assessment

## The Version 2.0 criteria

Under corrective action CA1, the investigation defined the intermediate acceptance criteria and the rules for judging against them. Corrective action CA1 then issues them in PCMP-001 Version 2.0, the master plan, effective `{python} REV2_DATE`. The investigation closed on `{python} CLOSED`, before that date, and the re-analysis in this section applied the rules as CA1 defined them.

Each drug-substance criterion is carried backward through the train, using the worst case each downstream step showed on the platform (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab). The platform worst case is the lowest fold clearance or the largest increase seen on those products. No margin is applied. The glycans keep their drug-substance criterion, because no downstream step changes them. Each viral clearance step is held to its platform claim. The claims sum to the cumulative clearance that the CQA register requires of the process, taken from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The sums are `{python} f"{xm_sum:.2f}"` against a requirement of `{python} f"{xm_req:g}"` log10 for XMuLV and `{python} f"{mvm_sum:.2f}"` against `{python} f"{mvm_req:g}"` log10 for MVM.

Corrective action CA1 also defined three rules that the re-analysis applies.

1. Verification compares each platform worst case with the A-Mab worst case that the response surface model of the downstream step predicts within its NOR. The bound that can replace a platform value is the one-sided `{python} VB` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high (the single-batch bound). Where the A-Mab prediction is worse than the platform value, the single-batch bound replaces it and the criteria upstream tighten. Where the single-batch bound is better than the platform value, it replaces it and the criteria upstream widen, but only if the model passes the adequacy tests of PCMP-001 Version 2.0 (R² less predicted R² at most `{python} f"{MAX_GAP:g}"`, and no lack of fit at the `{python} f"{LOF_ALPHA:g}"` level). Otherwise the platform value stands. No criterion is set from a point prediction or from a confidence bound of the mean.
2. A scale-down model is qualified for an output when its offset (the mean of the scale-down set-point runs less the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches) is known precisely enough that the conclusion over the NOR is the same at either end of the `{python} OFF_CI` % confidence interval of the offset. A qualified model may differ in mean from manufacturing scale. Every Version 2.0 judgement subtracts the offset, so results are stated at manufacturing scale.
3. A quality attribute is judged per batch, on the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch. Viral clearance is judged on the mean predicted log reduction factor (LRF) at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the other parameters.

@tbl-iac gives the `{python} n_iac` criteria with their derivation. Of these, `{python} n_iac_ds` are the drug-substance criterion applied directly, `{python} n_iac_back` are carried back through the downstream steps, and `{python} n_iac_claim` are platform viral clearance claims. When the platform worst cases were verified (§6.2), `{python} n_tight` of the back-calculated criteria were tightened and `{python} n_wid` were widened. The criterion for `{python} both_txt` is counted in both, because one downstream step tightened it and another widened it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation().show()
```

This campaign's data enter the Version 2.0 criteria, as they entered the Version 1.0 criteria. The difference lies in how they enter. Version 1.0 set its criteria after the data were seen, from the nominal performance of the downstream steps, with a safety factor chosen step by step. Version 2.0 starts from the platform worst case, by a rule written before any report applied it. This campaign's data can then move a criterion only through the single-batch bound of a downstream step within its NOR, in either direction. The data of a step never set its own criterion.

## Verification of the platform worst cases

The platform worst cases are assumptions about A-Mab. Each was checked against the data of the downstream step it describes, under the first rule of CA1 in §6.1. The value observed at the edges of the characterization range is shown for information. @tbl-iac-verification gives the result. Of the `{python} n_ver` assumptions that could be tested, `{python} n_ver_met` were confirmed, because the prediction within the NOR was no worse than the platform value. For `{python} n_ver_wsup` of them the single-batch bound was also better than the platform value, on an adequate model, and the criteria upstream were recalculated with the bound. `{python} vin_sentence` For the other `{python} nw(n_ver_kept)` the single-batch bound was not better than the platform value, so the platform value stands.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.worst_case_verification().show()
```

At the edges of the characterization range, cation exchange cleared host cell protein `{python} f1(cex_hcp_edge)`-fold, short of the platform worst case of `{python} f1(cex_hcp_assumed)`-fold. Within the NOR, the lowest clearance the model predicts is `{python} f1(cex_hcp_nor)`-fold, and the single-batch bound is `{python} f1(cex_hcp_bound)`-fold. The edges of the characterization range lie outside the NOR, so the edge value does not decide the criterion. The prediction within the NOR confirms the platform value. The single-batch bound is below it, so the platform value of `{python} f1(cex_hcp_assumed)`-fold stands for cation exchange. The verification used the models that `{python} INV2["id"]` corrective action CA3 selects for each output (§2). At anion exchange, the single-batch bound for host cell protein is `{python} T.num(aex_hcp_bound)`-fold, which is better than the platform value of `{python} T.num(aex_hcp_assumed)`-fold. The anion exchange model passes the adequacy tests, so this bound replaced the platform value. The anion exchange bound widened the cation exchange criterion for host cell protein from `{python} T.num(cex_hcp_apriori)` to `{python} T.num(cex_hcp_v2)` ng/mg. Carried back through the platform value at cation exchange and this bound at anion exchange, the Protein A criterion for host cell protein was widened from `{python} big(pa_hcp_apriori)` to `{python} big(pa_hcp_v2)` ng/mg. The Protein A criterion is also wider than the Version 1.0 limit of `{python} big(pa_hcp_crit)` ng/mg, which was never an approved criterion (finding F1). In all, `{python} n_wid` criteria were widened, for `{python} wid_list`. @tbl-par-change in §6.3 gives the ranges that widened as a result.

One assumption was not confirmed. The platform worst case for aggregate at cation exchange is a fold clearance of `{python} f1(cex_agg_assumed)`. Within its NOR, the lowest fold clearance the response surface model of this campaign predicts is `{python} f2(cex_agg_nor)`, and the single-batch bound is `{python} f2(cex_agg_bound)`. The aggregate criteria upstream of cation exchange were recalculated with the bound, and the `{python} n_tight` aggregate criteria at the `{python} tight_steps` steps were tightened. At the bioreactor the same criterion was also widened, because the single-batch bound of the aggregate increase at low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} f2(vi_agg_bound)` percentage points, is smaller than the platform value of `{python} f2(vi_agg_assumed)`. The platform value is an increase over a hold of `{python} plat_hold_min` min. The A-Mab value is an increase within the NOR as characterized, where the hold lasts at most `{python} f"{amab_hold_max:g}"` min. `{python} vi_why_text` The criterion is still right, because routine manufacture does not hold longer than the NOR. The acidic-variant increase at low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} f2(vi_acid_bound)` points, is also below its platform value of `{python} f2(vi_acid_assumed)`, but its model fits exactly, so the bioreactor criterion for acidic variants stays at its a priori value. `{python} tight_phrase`

The criterion of `{python} T.num(lpa_crit)` ppm for leached Protein A at the Protein A step rests on two platform worst cases, for cation exchange and anion exchange, that no response of this campaign could test (not a response in @tbl-iac-verification). Together they assume a clearance of `{python} f1(lpa_assumed)`-fold. Judged per batch at manufacturing scale, the upper 95 % prediction limit for the Protein A pool is at most `{python} f2(lpa_hi)` ppm over the NOR (@tbl-results). It meets the step criterion. For a batch at that level to meet the drug-substance criterion of `{python} f"{ds_lpa:g}"` ppm, the downstream steps need to clear only `{python} f2(lpa_need)`-fold. The untested platform worst cases therefore carry little of the weight of this criterion.

## Impact by document

All `{python} n_docs_v1` documents in @tbl-docs are to be reissued at Version 2.0, effective `{python} REV2_DATE`. Corrective action CA1 reissues the master plan PCMP-001 with the criteria and rules of §6.1. Corrective action CA2 amends the step plans PCP-003 to PCP-010 to state the criteria with their basis. Corrective action CA3 reissues the step reports, the master report PCMR-001, the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001 and the Pre-Characterization Risk Assessment RA-001. The step reports judge each step against the criteria, on the models selected under `{python} inv2_id` (§2), and PCMR-001 consolidates the result. Of the `{python} n_par_changed` ranges that changed, `{python} n_par_wider` widened. Of these, `{python} brx_wider` are at the bioreactor. There, `{python} brx_wider_glycan` glycan ranges widened because the capability alert limits of Version 1.0 (finding F3) gave way to the drug-substance criteria. A further `{python} nw(brx_wider_agg)` aggregate ranges widened because the Version 1.0 aggregate limit, divided by a safety factor (finding F2), gave way to a back-calculated criterion with no margin. At the other steps, `{python} n_wider_other_r1` of the `{python} n_wider_other` wider ranges belong to criteria that Version 1.0 had divided by a safety factor. `{python} wider_rest_phrase`

At cation exchange, the Version 1.0 aggregate criterion of `{python} T.num(cex_agg_crit)` % HMW was the drug-substance criterion divided by a safety factor of `{python} f1(cex_agg_margin)`. Against it, the proven acceptable range for protein load, with the other parameters varying within their NORs, was `{python} cex_load_v1` g/L resin. That range did not reach the upper end of the protein load NOR at `{python} f"{cex_load_nor[1]:g}"` g/L resin. Against the Version 2.0 criterion of `{python} f"{cex_ds_agg_v2:g}"` %, the range is `{python} cex_load_v2` g/L resin, and it covers the upper end of the NOR. At the bioreactor, the range for dissolved CO2 judged on galactosylation, computed the same way, was `{python} brx_gal_v1` mmHg at Version 1.0. It did not reach the lower end of the NOR at `{python} f"{brx_co2_nor[0]:g}"` mmHg. Judged against the drug-substance criterion, it is `{python} brx_gal_v2` mmHg.

The ranges that did not widen have three causes. At the bioreactor, the only Version 2.0 limit stricter than its Version 1.0 counterpart is the lower limit for acidic variants, which Version 1.0 did not apply (finding F4, §4.5). As a result, `{python} nw(brx_acid_changed)` of the acidic variant ranges there changed. Of these, `{python} brx_acid_phrase`. Judged against the upper limit alone, every one of them would span the whole characterization range, so the lower limit of `{python} f"{ds_acid_lo:g}"` % now sets them. Acidic variants fall as `{python} acid_unc_name` rises, in this campaign's response surface model and in the response surface estimates of the published A-Mab case study [@amab2009, Table 3.16]. For `{python} acid_unc_name`, the range is therefore `{python} acid_unc_par` `{python} acid_unc_unit`, and it no longer reaches the upper end of the NOR at `{python} f"{acid_unc_nor_hi:g}"` `{python} acid_unc_unit`.

At low-pH viral inactivation, the XMuLV criterion rose from the Version 1.0 value of `{python} f2(vi_xm_v1)` log10 to the platform claim of `{python} f"{vi_xm_v2:g}"` log10, and XMuLV clearance is now judged at the least favourable combination of the other parameters. The XMuLV clearance of low-pH viral inactivation therefore no longer gives a proven acceptable range `{python} vi_none_phrase`. For inactivation pH, Version 1.0 had reported `{python} vi_ph_v1`. At anion exchange, the viral clearance criteria also rose to the platform claims and are also judged at the least favourable combination. The load pH ranges there narrowed slightly, for `{python} aex_narrow_txt`.

@tbl-results gives each pool attribute of each step against its Version 2.0 criterion over the NOR as characterized, at manufacturing scale. Each is judged on the 95 % prediction interval for a single batch, from the response surface model that Version 1.0 fitted (§2). `{python} qa_phrase`

The limit is therefore lowest at the corner of the NOR where `{python} acid_corner_txt`. `{python} acid_nsig_txt` With every parameter at its set-point the batch interval meets the criterion. ## Capability

In the re-analysis, the capability of acidic variants was assessed against both ends of its range (finding F4). The re-analysis uses the capability simulation that Version 1.0 reported, at the NOR as characterized. The lowest capability index of the drug substance moves from `{python} f2(v1_min_cpk)` for `{python} v1_min_name`, as PCMR-001 Version 1.0 printed it, to `{python} f2(v2_min_cpk)` for acidic variants, against the lower limit of `{python} f"{ds_acid_lo:g}"` %. PCMP-001 Version 2.0 sets a capability target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)`, which is common industry practice for a capable process. It sets a minimum of `{python} f2(CPK_MIN)`, the point at which a spread of three standard deviations reaches the criterion. `{python} thr_sentence` The re-analysis also gives the probability of a drug substance batch outside specification for each attribute, from the same simulation. For acidic variants the simulation puts `{python} noos_phrase` outside the range, and a normal fit gives `{python} big(acid_ppm)` per million. `{python} other_oos_phrase`

## Fragments

In the re-analysis, fragments are judged on nrCE-SDS results only, against the fragment criteria at the `{python} frag_steps_txt` steps in @tbl-iac. SEC fragment results from the Protein A pool and the low-pH viral inactivation pool will be reported for information only and not used to judge a step. They could not have supported a fragment criterion at those steps, because they include host cell protein (finding F6).

## Product impact

No GMP batch of A-Mab was manufactured or dispositioned on the basis of these documents, and Version 1.0 was not used in a regulatory submission. The findings concern how the characterization data were judged. The experiments and the drug-substance criteria that existed in Version 1.0 are unchanged. The process is unchanged except for NORs at the `{python} proc_nor_steps` steps and set-points at `{python} proc_sp_steps`, which PCR-005 and PCR-006 Version 2.0 change (§2, §6.3). Version 2.0 adds one drug-substance criterion, for fragments, at `{python} T.crit(0, ds_frag, "upper")` %. There is no product impact.

# Corrective and preventive actions

The actions in @tbl-capa follow from the root cause and the contributing causes in §5. All `{python} n_capa` actions were open at closure and are tracked to their due dates in the CAPA system [@ichq10].

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(capa_md,
        caption=f"Corrective (CA) and preventive (PA) actions. Every action was {capa_status}.",
        label="tbl-capa",
        header={"Owner function": "Owner\nfunction"},
        align=["l", "P{8.4cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "l"]).show()
```

Corrective action CA1, the reissue of the master plan PCMP-001 with a priori criteria, removes the root cause for this campaign. It also answers the contributing cause that no document defined how much less a downstream step may clear within its NOR. PCMP-001 Version 2.0 fixes every step criterion before any study is judged against it, defines the downstream worst case each criterion protects against, and lets no step's data set its own criterion. Corrective action CA2, the amendment of the step plans with the criteria and the fragment method, brings the decision `{python} AMD["id"]` to measure fragments by nrCE-SDS into the plans (finding F6). Corrective action CA3 reissues the reports. They judge each step against the new criteria, on the models selected under `{python} inv2_id` (§2), and assess the capability of acidic variants against both ends of their range (finding F4).

Preventive action PA1, the revision of SOP-1002 so that acceptance criteria are approved in the protocol before execution, removes the root cause for future campaigns. It also removes the contributing cause that SOP-1002 did not require this. Preventive action PA2 adds to the report review checklist a check that every acceptance criterion can be traced to the approved protocol. That check would have detected the criteria added after approval (finding F1). Preventive action PA3 records execution dates and calibration status in every study record. It answers the contributing cause that no second review checked the dates in the title blocks and study records (finding F5).

Two causes have no preventive action. No action adds a second review of whether a capability calculation uses the one-sided or two-sided criterion that the register gives. Corrective action CA3, which reissues the reports with a two-sided assessment of acidic variants, corrects finding F4 for this campaign only. For this product, the two-sided assessment is fixed in PCMP-001 Version 2.0, so the error cannot recur in this campaign. No action creates a procedure that would require a method decision to be assessed against the approved plans and put into effect by plan amendment either. Corrective action CA2 brings the decision `{python} AMD["id"]` into the plans, but a future method decision would again depend on the people involved to reach the documents.

# Effectiveness check

The corrective actions are verified effective when the Version 2.0 package is effective and QA has repeated the review that triggered this investigation, on PCMR-001 Version 2.0, the master report. That review checks three things. Every step criterion used in a proven acceptable range analysis must appear in PCMP-001 Version 2.0 with its basis, and no criterion may be set by data from the step it judges. Every fragment result used to judge a step must be by nrCE-SDS. Every study must carry its execution window.

QA verifies the preventive actions by `{python} eff_due`. The check requires `{python} eff_crit`. QA owns both checks.

# Conclusion and closure

The investigation confirmed the classification as `{python} INV["classification"]`. The criteria used to support the operating ranges in a BLA were not defined before the data were seen. The analyses that rested on them could therefore not be relied on as approved. The investigation found no product impact (§6.6).

The corrective actions are due with Version 2.0 on `{python} ca_open_due`, and the preventive actions by `{python} pa_due_max`. `{python} DOC` was closed on `{python} CLOSED`, with its remaining actions open and tracked to completion under the effectiveness check in §8.
